homilies.title: 單-常年期第1週星期五道理：以信德與犧牲彼此代禱
homilies.content:
祈禱是我們每天的功課，對我們而言並不陌生，正如身體需要空氣，靈魂也需要祈禱。然而，很多時候，我們沒有力量祈禱，或因懶惰，或覺得天主的恩寵不夠。在那個時候，我們實在一點也不想祈禱，祈禱成了負擔，只想什麼都不做。

因此，讓我們不要忘記，我們也需要別人幫助我們祈禱，就如他們為我們送來氧氣瓶，使我們的靈魂重新充滿新鮮的空氣。

今天的福音說：耶穌正向他們講道時，有人帶著一個癱子到祂跟前，由四個人抬著。

當我們軟弱無力時，就像這個癱子；而那四個人，就是一直為我們祈禱的人。

接著，他們在耶穌所在之處上方拆開屋頂，開了一個洞。這告訴我們，幫助朋友不能只是口頭說說，而要把助人的決心付諸實行；在這個過程中，我們也需要作出一些犧牲。

最後，耶穌看見他們的信德，不但治好了癱子，也赦免了他的罪。這裡所指的不是病人的信德，而是抬他來的人所具有的信德；因為有時候，一個人會因另一個人的信德而獲得治癒，也就是因朋友的信德而得到幫助。

別人的信德竟然有如此大的影響，使這人立刻站起來，身心都得到治癒，並因一人的功勞，使另一人的罪得到赦免。由此可見，每個人自身的信德，在天主前具有何等重要的分量。

願聖母使我們明白，犧牲也是幫助他人不可缺少的一部分。

en.title: Odd-Friday of the First Week in Ordinary Time: Faith, Sacrifice, and Praying for One Another
en.content:
Prayer is a daily task for us. It is not new to us, just as the body needs air, and the soul needs prayer. But very often, we don't have the strength to pray, or we are lazy, or or we feel that God's graces is not enough. At that time, we really don't want to pray at all, prayer becomes a burden and we just want to do nothing.

So let's not forget that we also need other people to help us pray, just as they help us to bring oxygen tank to fill our souls with new air.

In today's Gospel: Jesus was preaching the word to them when some people came bringing him a paralytic carried by four men.

When we are powerless, we are like this paralytic. And these four men were the ones who always prayed for us.

And then they stripped the roof over the place where Jesus was, and they had made an opening. it is telling us that in order to help a friend, it is not just a matter of talking about it but of practising our determination to help, and that this process requires some sacrifice on our part.

In the end Jesus Seeing their faith not only healed the paralytic but also forgave him his sins. He did not mean the faith of the sick man, but of his bearers; for it sometimes happens that a man is healed by the faith of another. Or we say the faith of our friends.

It may indeed be seen how much each person's own faith weighs with God, when that of another had such influence that the whole man at once rose up , healed body and soul, and by one man's merit, The sins of another should be forgiven.

May Our Lady make us understand that sacrifice is also a necessary part of helping people.

homilies.title: 單-常年期第2週星期三道理：伸出手來，領受主的仁慈
homilies.content:
猶太人指責主的門徒在安息日掐取麥穗充飢，因此主以達味的事例，使他們明白其中的真理；接著又藉一個奇蹟，向他們顯明祂所做的，是為實現安息日的真義，而不是破壞安息日。主告訴我們，在安息日為人的健康而施行奇蹟，是虔敬的行為；在安息日為身體的健康而行事，並不是壞事。

因此，既然主如此教導，我們的主日彌撒也是我們的安息日。若是為了照顧病人，我們便可免除相關的責任。

法利賽人知道耶穌會治好那人，便故意向祂挑戰。於是，耶穌含怒環視他們。

祂含怒環視他們，並因他們的盲目而憂傷，這符合祂的人性，也顯示耶穌願意承擔我們的痛苦。祂要向我們顯示祂的話語何等有力，並證明祂就是生活的聖言。正如天主以一句話創造萬有，耶穌也要藉自己的話語施行奇蹟：

於是，祂對那人說：「伸出手來！」

「他一伸出來，他的手就復了原。」耶穌藉這些事回答門徒，同時也表明祂的生命高於法律。祂要藉自己的話語，賜給人更豐盛的生命。

但從奧祕的角度來看，那個手枯乾的人，代表人在善行上結果子的能力已經枯萎，如今卻藉著上主的仁慈而獲得治癒。

當我們的原祖父母摘取禁樹的果實時，人的手便枯乾了；而救主在十字架的木上伸出祂無罪的手，藉祂的恩寵，使這隻手重新得到善行的滋養，恢復健康。

最後，讓我們反省：我們是否有時也像法利賽人一樣，看待耶穌在我們生命中的安排？我們是否也覺得，主不應當如此安排，因為這樣會違反我們自己所定的規則？

願聖母帶領我們，明白上主對我們的愛。

en.title: Odd-Wednesday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time: Stretch Out Your Hand and Receive the Lord’s Mercy
en.content:
The Jews accused the Lord's disciples of plucking ears of corn on the Sabbath to feed their hunger, so the Lord used the example of David to make them understand the truth, and then showed them by a miracle that he was doing it for the truth of the Sabbath and not to destroy it. The Lord tells us that it is a pious act to perform miracles on the Sabbath for the health of the people, and that it is not a bad thing to do on the Sabbath for the health of the body.

So because the Lord has said so, our Sunday Mass is also our Sabbath. If we take care of the sick we are exempt from responsibility.

So the Pharisees knew that Jesus would heal him and they challenged him on purpose. So Jesus looked angrily round at them.

He looked angrily round at them, saddened by their blindness, which is in keeping with human nature and Jesus' willingness to bear our suffering. He wants to show us how powerful his words are and how he wants to prove that he is the living Word. Just as God created all things with one word, so Jesus wants to do miracles with his word:

So he said to the man, 'Stretch out your hand.

"He stretched it out and his hand was better.". Jesus answered the disciples through these things, and at the same time made it clear that his life was higher than the law. And by his words he would give people a richer life.

But from a mystical point of view, the man with the withered hand represents a human being whose fruitfulness in good works had dried up, but who is now healed through the mercy of the Lord;

the human hand, which had dried up when our first parents plucked the fruit of the forbidden tree, was restored to health through the sap of good works by the grace of the Saviour, who stretched out his sinless hand on the tree of the cross.

Finally, let us reflect on whether we sometimes look at what Jesus has ordained in our lives in the same way as the Pharisees? Do we not also feel that the Lord should not have arranged this in such a way that it would violate our own law?

May Our Lady lead us to understand the love of the Lord for us.

homilies.title: 單-常年期第3週星期五道理：天國的種子與自由意志
homilies.content:
《天主教教理》告訴我們，教會有三種狀態：「旅途中的教會」，或稱「戰鬥的教會」；已到達天堂、享有天主光榮的「凱旋的教會」；以及仍在煉獄中受苦、等待進入天堂的「受苦的教會」。這三者是同一個教會，只是處於不同的狀態。

今天福音中的天國比喻，是在講論教會。主以這個比喻談論那些得救的人，所以經上說：「天主的國好比一個人把種子撒在地裏。」不論黑夜白天，他或睡或起，種子發芽生長，至於怎樣，他卻不知道。

天主的國就是教會。教會由天主管理，也治理人，並克服那些反對她的勢力與一切邪惡。天主的國確實就像一個人撒種。這個人就是耶穌：祂是天主，也是天主子；祂保持自己的天主性不變而成為人，將種子撒在地上，也就是藉著使人認識天主的聖言，光照整個世界。

種子是耶穌的話，是生命的話；土地是人的心；那人的睡眠，則代表救主的死亡。種子日夜發芽生長，因為在基督安眠之後，基督徒的人數不斷增加；無論經歷災難或順境，他們的信德都日益茁壯，行為也在磨難與順境之後繼續成長。

關於「至於怎樣，他卻不知道」，主是在作一個比喻：祂不讓我們預先知道，我們當中誰會結果實，直到最後才會顯明。這也是提醒我們，要奮鬥到底。

或者，更確切地說，祂說「至於怎樣，他卻不知道」，是為了顯明領受聖言之人的自由意志。因為天主願意人自由地與祂的旨意合作，而不是由天主親自控制人，使人完成祂所有的意願，以免人誤以為天主早已預定了人的命運。

願聖母帶領我們，明白自由意志的真正意義。

en.title: Odd-Friday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time: The Seed of the Kingdom and Free Will
en.content:
The Catechism tells us that there are three states of the Church: the  (Pilgrim Church), or "Church Militant", and the (Church Triumphant), which has reached heaven and is enjoying the glory of God, and the "Church Suffering" , which is still suffering in purgatory and awaiting its ascension to heaven. These three are the same church,But different states

In today's Gospel, the parable of the Kingdom of God is talking about the Church.He puts forth a parable concerning those only who are saved.Wherefore it is said, “This is what the kingdom of God is like. A man throws seed on the land.”Night and day, while he sleeps, when he is awake, the seed is sprouting and growing; how, he does not know.

The kingdom of God is the Church, which is ruled by God, rules over men herself, and steps down the forces that are opposed (əˈpəʊzd)to her and all evil.The kingdom of God indeed is as if a man should throw seed. This man is Jesus he is God and the Son of God, having without change been and become man, has cast seed upon the earth, that is saying, He has enlightened the whole world by the word of divine knowledge.

The seed is the word of Jesus is word of live, the ground is the human heart, and the sleep of the man means the death of the Saviour. The seed springs up night and day, because after the sleep of Christ, the number of Christians, through calamity (kəˈlæməti) and prosperity (prɒˈsperəti) , continued to flourish more and more in faith, and grow in deeds after the tribulation and prosperity.

Regarding the "how, he does not know", he is making an analogy( əˈnælədʒi ); that is, he does not let us know who among us will bear fruit until the end.It is also a reminder to us  to fight to the end.

Or rather, He said "how, He does not know" to show the free will of those who receive the Word, for God wills that man should cooperate freely with His will, not that God Himself should control man in the accomplishment of all His will, lest men should misunderstand that God has predestinated the destiny of man.

May Our Lady lead us to understand the true meaning of free will.

homilies.title: 單-常年期第4週星期五道理：復活的盼望與面見天主
homilies.content:
今天的福音說：有人說：「洗者若翰從死者中復活了，因此才有這些奇能在他身上運行。」

我們信仰的基礎是復活，但我們對復活究竟認識多少呢？

有些人可能以為，復活就是享有極大的肉身快樂，或過著無憂無慮的生活。然而，最大的幸福並不在這些事上。正如聖經告訴我們：天主的國不在於吃喝；到了復活的時候，男女也不娶不嫁。

最大的幸福是面對面看見天主。有人可能會問，為什麼面對面看見天主就是最大的幸福呢？我們都有不明白事情的經驗，也都希望知道更多，好能做得更多，或解決更多問題。面對面看見天主，就是使我們無限的求知渴望得到滿足。藉著瞻仰無限的天主，我們彷彿能對萬事有無限更深的認識，也彷彿能把更多事情做得正確。

聖巴拉斯在被祝聖為主教之前，是一位具有奇妙醫治能力的醫師。許多奇蹟被歸於他的代禱，其中包括他在避難期間治癒患病野獸的事蹟，因此他也成為野生動物的主保。到了第六世紀，東方已尊他為喉疾患者的主保；在西方，這項敬禮則見於第九世紀。

自第十六世紀開始，聖巴拉斯的祝福禮至今仍在許多地方於他的慶日舉行。兩支蠟燭經祝福後，在會眾面前交叉放置；或以在油中祝聖的燈芯，觸碰信友的喉嚨。

願聖母堅固我們對復活的信德！

en.title: Odd-Friday of the Fourth Week in Ordinary Time: The Hope of Resurrection and Seeing God Face to Face
en.content:
In today’s Gospel:Some were saying, ‘John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and that is why miraculous powers are at work in him.

The foundation of our faith is the resurrection, but how much do we know about it?

Some may think that it is about the great sense of physical pleasure. Or a life free from worry. But the greatest happiness is not in these things, as the Bible tells us: because the kingdom of God does not mean eating or drinking, for at the resurrection men and women do not marry.

The greatest happiness is to see God face to face. Some may wonder why seeing God face to face is the greatest happiness. We all have the experience of ignorance, of wanting to know more, so we can do more or solve more. To see God face to face is to satisfy our infinite desire to know. By seeing the infinite God, we can become as if we know infinitely more about everything, and we can also become as if we can do infinitely more right.

before Blaise was made bishop, he was a physician possessed of wonderful healing power. Numerous miracles were attributedəˈtrɪbjuːtɪd  to him, including ɪnˈkluːdɪŋ the cure of diseased beasts during his refuge, thus accounting for his also being the patron saint of wild animals. He was venerated as the patron of sufferers from throat diseases in the East by the 6th century and in the West by the 9th century.

Begun in the 16th century, the blessing of St. Blaise is a ceremonyˈserəməni still practiced and celebrated on his feast day in many places. Two candles are consecrated and crossed before the congregation; or a wick, consecrated in oil, is touched to the throats of the faithful.

May Our Lady strengthen our faith in the Resurrection!

homilies.title: 單-常年期第5週星期五道理：厄法達，開了罷
homilies.content:
有人給耶穌帶來一個又聾又啞的人，求祂給他覆手。耶穌領他離開群眾，來到一旁。

耶穌不願公開施行奇蹟，是為教導我們，一切奇蹟都來自天主。祂把手指放進那人的耳朵，是要顯示天主的第二位與人的肉身結合，因此祂所做的一切，都與天主的德能有關。

也正因為亞當的過犯，人類的肢體與感官遭受許多痛苦，基督才來到世界，在自己身上顯示人性的完美。因此，祂用手指開啟人的耳朵，並藉自己的唾液賜下說話的能力。

祂要顯示，祂聖體上的所有肢體都是神聖的，甚至連使舌結鬆開的唾液也是如此。因為唾液不過是身體多餘的水分，但在上主內，一切都是聖的。

然後，祂望天嘆息，向那人說：「厄法達！」就是說：「開了罷！」

祂同時嘆息，是因為祂承擔了我們所犯的一切罪，憐憫人類，也看見人類正遭受罪惡的污染。

那人的耳朵便開了，舌結也解了，說話也清楚了。耶穌囑咐他們，不要把這事告訴任何人。祂藉此教導我們，不要誇耀自己的能力，而要以自己的十字架與屈辱為榮。祂也要求他們隱瞞這個奇蹟，以免猶太人因嫉妒而在祂的時辰未到之前，便想殺害祂。

願聖母帶領我們，開啟以天主的眼光看事物的窗戶。

en.title: Odd-Friday of the Fifth Week in Ordinary Time: Ephphatha, Be Opened
en.content:
They brought him a deaf man who had an impediment in his speech; and they asked him to lay his hand on him.  He took him aside in private, away from the crowd.

Jesus did not want to do miracles in public in order to teach us that all miracles come from God. When he put his finger in his ear, it was to show that the second person of God's Divine nature was united with human flesh, so that everything he did was related to divine virtue.

It was also because of Adam's transgression that humanity suffered so much in its members and senses and that Christ came into the world, that he showed in himself the perfection of humanity and thus opened the ear with his finger and gave power of speech with his saliva.

He wants to show that all the members of His holy body are divine, even the saliva that loosens the cords of the tongue. For saliva is only the excess water of the body, but in the Lord all things are holy.

Then looking up to heaven he sighed; and he said to him, ‘Ephphatha’, that is, ‘Be opened.

He sighs at the same time because he takes upon himself all the sins we commit, he has compassion on humanity and sees the pollution of sin that it is suffering.

And his ears were opened, and the ligament of his tongue was loosened and he spoke clearly. And Jesus ordered them to tell no one about it.By this He teaches us not to boast in our own power, but in our cross and humiliation. He also asked them to conceal this miracle, lest he should provoke the Jews to kill him before his time out of envy.

May Our Lady lead us to open the window of divine vision

homilies.title: 單-常年期第6週星期五道理：背起十字架，跟隨基督
homilies.content:
也許我們都聽過那個為了方便而鋸短自己十字架的人的故事。他為了方便，把原本的十字架鋸短了。因為拋棄了「對自己沒有用處的壓力」，他的生活變得比較輕鬆。

結果如何呢？他不斷減輕自己的十字架，過著快樂、順遂的生活，或許還被人稱為聰明人。但後來發生了一件令人悲傷的事：有一天，他來到天主面前，卻發現自己與天主相隔甚遠。上主對他說：「把你的十字架放下來罷！這樣你就能到我這裡來。」可惜，他的十字架已經太短了。我們都能想像，他後來會有怎樣的結果。

今天的福音告訴我們：

人縱然賺得了全世界，卻賠上了自己的生命，究竟有什麼益處呢？

耶穌彷彿在說：不要以為逃避十字架危險的人，就救了自己的靈魂。因為一個人若交出自己的靈魂、自己的生命，藉此賺得全世界，靈魂卻正在喪亡，他究竟得到了什麼？難道他還有另一個靈魂可以交換嗎？人可以用房屋的價款換取一棟房屋，但當他失去自己的靈魂時，就沒有另一個靈魂可以交付了。

背十字架是痛苦的，但我們仍應背負它。因為即使我們不願意背，它仍然存在於我們的生活中。若我們現在不背，將來仍要背負。

令人欣慰的是，我們是與耶穌一起背十字架，而祂將在未來賜給我們永恆的安慰。正如經上所說：「誰若願意跟隨我，該棄絕自己，背著自己的十字架，跟隨我……必要救得自己的生命。」

背起十字架之後，我們也需要獲得新的力量。重要的是，我們必須跟隨耶穌。因為人可能承受了痛苦，卻沒有跟隨基督，那麼他的痛苦便成了徒然。

因此，那些在看見天主的國帶著威能來到以前，決不會嘗到死味的人，究竟是誰呢？會是我們嗎？

願聖母幫助我們，看見十字架的真正意義。

en.title: Odd-Friday of the Sixth Week in Ordinary Time: Take Up Your Cross and Follow Christ
en.content:
Maybe we have all heard the story of the man who sawed off his cross for convenience. He sawed off his original cross for convenience. His life was easier because it threw away "the pressure that was not useful to him".

what is the result? He lived a life of constant reduction of the cross, a life of happiness, a life of good fortune, as one might say, as a wise man. But then a sad thing happened, one day he came to God, and he was so far away from God. The Lord said to him, "Put down your cross! Then you can come to me. Unfortunately, his cross was too short. We can all imagine what happened to him afterwards.

The gospel today tells us:

What gain, then, is it for a man to win the whole world and ruin his life?

Jesus seems to be saying, "Do not think that the man who avoids the danger of the cross has saved his soul; for when a man gives his soul, his life, and thereby gains the whole world, but his soul is perishing, what has he gained? Does he have another soul to replace it? A man may exchange the price of his house for a house, but when he loses his soul, he has no other soul to give.

Carrying the cross is painful, but we should carry it. Because even if we don't want to carry it, it is still in our lives. If we don't carry it now, we will have to carry it in the future.

The happy thing is that we are carrying the cross with Jesus. And He will give us eternal comfort in the future. As the Scripture says:‘If anyone wants to be a follower of mine, let him renounce himself and take up his cross and follow me......will save it。

After carrying the cross, we must be given new strength. It is important that we follow Jesus. For it may happen that a person may suffer and not follow Christ, so that person's suffering is in vain.

therefore, who are those , will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God come with power?Are we?

May Our Lady help us to see the true meaning of the cross

homilies.title: Have Faith in God (Mark 11:11–26)
homilies.content:
When we buy a mobile phone, we usually choose a durable one over a phone with better features but less durability. The same goes for purchasing computers, air conditioners, and even cars or bicycles. We care about how long they can be used and if they are likely to be easily damaged. The same applies to us as individuals. We should seek knowledge that can lead us and endure for a long time, knowledge that is universally applicable now and in the future.

If we find such knowledge, we will be like the generous men mentioned in today's reading: their good works have not been forgotten, and their glory will not fade. These are the virtuous people praised here.

In today's Gospel, the most important virtue is emphasized: faith.

Jesus was hungry. He saw a lush fig tree in the distance and approached it to see if he could find something on it. However, when he reached it, apart from leaves, he found nothing. So he cursed the tree, saying, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again!"

The purpose of Jesus' action was to strengthen the disciples' faith. The Lord is willing to bless everyone and does not desire to punish anyone, but at the same time, He wants His disciples to know that He has the power to judge. He saw the fig tree, which represents the Jews, having leaves, The Lord desires them to seek good deeds and bear fruit. He has taught, reproached, and performed miracles, but all these could not awaken their ignorance, so they deserve condemnation. However, our lord does not want to manifest this directly in people, so He demonstrated this power through the plant.

Finally, Jesus answered them, saying, "Have faith in God. I tell you solemnly,  and said:everything you ask and pray for, believe that you have it already, and it will be yours." Because those who sincerely believe, lifting their hearts to God and joining with Him, will feel a burning conviction that they have received what they asked for. Because those who interceding

/ ˌɪntəˈsiːdɪŋ / with tears, feel as if they are holding onto the feet of the Lord in prayer, they will receive what they have rightly asked for. Additionally, forgiving others is a condition for our prayers to be answered. As the Lord said, "Therefore, if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there in front of the altar. First, go and be reconciled to them; then come and offer your gift."

It's as if Jesus is telling us: Do you want to receive all the graces you need through prayer? Approach with a willing heart and you will obtain everything.

May the Blessed Virgin Mary help us increase our faith so that our faith may be pleasing to God.

homilies.title: 單-常年期第22週星期五道理：禁食、愛德與敞開自我
homilies.content:
若翰的門徒來到耶穌跟前，說：「為什麼我們和法利賽人都禁食，而祢的門徒卻不禁食呢？」

洗者若翰的門徒從心裡相信若翰的話，也知道若翰曾譴責法利賽人，並尊重耶穌。

耶穌明白他們話語背後的意思：他們不是要譴責耶穌，而是真心想知道，為什麼祂的門徒沒有經常禁食。

其實，若翰的門徒想說的是：主啊，祢是靈性的醫師，祢不禁食是自然的事，但祢的門徒為什麼也不禁食呢？

首先，我們必須知道，洗者若翰不喝淡酒和烈酒，是要藉著禁食加強節制，並藉節制增長功勞與德行。然而，耶穌是天上的天主，是新以色列的新郎，具有無限的能力，是德行的主，也是赦免罪過者。

因此，門徒為什麼不能因著耶穌而與罪人一起吃飯，並藉此獲得正義與德行呢？不與罪人一起吃飯，反而會缺少愛德。基督禁食，是為教導我們禁食與祈禱的重要；祂與罪人一起吃飯，則是為彰顯祂的能力與恩惠。

禁食是可取的，但作為向天主表達虔敬的方式，並不是對每一個人、在每一個時刻都合適，例如赴婚宴時就不適宜。每個人的處境都不同：在同一時刻，有人喜樂，也有人悲傷。每個人都只能在自己的處境與時間裡，以自己獨特的方式與天主建立關係。

我們快樂時可以讚美天主，悲傷時也可以向祂哭訴。即使同樣是引領罪人悔改，耶穌與若翰的做法也不同：一位藉友誼與罪人吃喝，另一位則以身作則，要求他們禁食悔改。唯有不再以自己的標準衡量別人，我們才能與萬民之父相遇，並發現天主遠遠超過我們在小井底所見的那一小片天空。

願聖母幫助我們敞開自我，專心聆聽每一位弟兄姊妹的需要。

en.title: Odd-Friday of the Twenty-Second Week in Ordinary Time: Fasting, Charity, and Opening Ourselves to Others
en.content:
John's disciples came to Jesus and said, 'Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not?

The disciples of John the Baptist believed John's words from the heart, and knew that John condemned the Pharisees and respected Jesus.

Jesus knew the meaning behind their words, not to condemn Jesus, but really to find out why His disciples did not fast regularly.

In fact, what John's disciples were trying to say was: Lord, it is natural that you, as a spiritual physician, should not fast, but why do your disciples not fast?

First of all, we need to know that the reason John the Baptist did not drink light and strong wine was to increase his abstinence by fasting. It was to increase his merit and virtue by abstinence. But Jesus is the God of heaven, the Bridegroom of the new Israel, infinitely powerful, the Lord of virtue, and the forgiver of sins.

So why not eat with sinners because of Jesus, so that His disciples can gain righteousness and virtue by doing so? It would have been without of charity not to eat with sinners. Christ fasted in order to teach us the importance of fasting and prayer, and he ate with sinners in order to show us his power and favour.

Fasting is desirable, but as a way of showing devotion to God, it is not appropriate for everyone at all times, for example, not when attending a wedding feast. Everyone's situation is different: at the same moment, some people rejoice, others grieve. Each person can only relate to God in his or her own unique way, in his or her own situation and time.

We can praise God when we are happy and we can cry to Him when we are sad. Even in the same way of bringing sinners to repentance, Jesus and John did it differently: one ate and drank with sinners through friendship, and the other asked them to fast and repent through example. It is only when we stop measuring others by our own standards that we can meet the Father of all men and discover that God is much more than the small piece of sky we see at the bottom of little wells.

May Our Lady help us to open our egos to hear only the needs of every brothers and sisters.

homilies.title: 常年期第30週星期三道理：竭力由窄門而入
homilies.content:
在祈禱當中，禮儀本身就是祈禱，宣認信仰的適當場所就是在舉行敬天禮儀中，即彌撒聖事，這是不可取代的最高超的祈禱。任何祈禱都沒有在彌撒中所得到的恩寵與效果更大。

所以對於基督徒的操守是不可替代的條件就如參與教會的禮儀要求信德一樣，如果信的不表現在行為上，就是死的，這樣的信德也不能結出永生的果實。

今天福音中:

有一個人問他說：「主！得救的人果然不多嗎？」耶穌對眾人說：你們竭力由窄門而入吧！

窄門也代表聖者們的辛勞與苦難。因為有怎樣的工作就可以證實有怎樣的能力，所以怎樣的忍受勞苦和試探他就是怎樣的人。

可是，主耶穌在其他地方所說的 "我的軛是柔和的，我的擔子是輕省的 "又是什麼意思呢？怎麼跟這裡講要很痛苦有點不一樣。其實這部矛盾。

其實前面所說的是正在接受試探的情況而說，而後面是因戰勝試探的人而說的。在人來說，凡是麻煩、困難的事，但只要用心去做，一切困難也可變得簡單。

所以，雖然救恩的路，起初是狹窄的，但通過它便可進入一個光明的彼岸，相反，寬闊的路會導致傷亡。

這裡我們要想耶穌對那些人為什麼這樣說，不直接說明多或少。因為主的回答，不只是聽那些人要問甚麼，而更是考慮到對他的聽眾是否能得到益處。所以知道得救的人是多還是少，對他的聽眾有什麼益處呢?當然沒有甚麼益處。

但如果回答使人知道人得救的途徑，那主自然便是這樣回答。因此，他故意不回答這個沒意思的問題，而是把他的話語轉向一個更重要的話題。

願聖母使我們了解天主的心意，使我們的祈禱時時得到主的悅納。
